entities.summary:
Wadjenes, also known as Wadjlas, Ougotlas and Tlas, was an early Egyptian king who may have ruled during the 2nd Dynasty. The 2nd Dynasty is considered the Old Kingdom period of Ancient Egypt, which is believed to have lasted from circa 2890 to 2686 BC. The region of Egypt is located in Northeast Africa, bordering the Mediterranean Sea to the north and the Red Sea to the east. The Old Kingdom period is significant because it was during this time that the pyramids were built, including the Great Pyramid of Giza, which is one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World. The 2nd Dynasty is also notable for the reign of Pharaohs Khasekhemwy and Senedjem I, who played important roles in the development of the Egyptian civilization.

The significance of Wadjenes lies in the mystery surrounding his identity and the possibility that he may have ruled during a time when the Egyptian kingdom was still consolidating its power. The name Wadjenes is not contemporarily attested as the name of a king, but it frequently appears in Ramesside kinglists, which are lists of Egyptian pharaohs compiled during the New Kingdom period. Egyptologists continue to study these kinglists to gain a better understanding of the early dynasties and the evolution of the Egyptian monarchy.

Despite the uncertainty surrounding his identity, Wadjenes is an important figure in the study of Ancient Egyptian history and the development of the Egyptian monarchy. His reign may have marked the beginning of a new period of Egyptian history, one that was characterized by the rise of the Old Kingdom and the construction of the pyramids.

The legacy of Wadjenes can be seen in the continued study of Ancient Egyptian history and the ongoing efforts to decipher the Ramesside kinglists. His significance also extends to the field of Egyptology, where his name is often mentioned alongside other important figures in the study of Ancient Egypt.
